title: I built "w-bonkers": an agent-installable pipeline that runs my NSE stock plan on rails. My todo app is the approval button.
author: Somchandra17

comments.author: kratos01
comments.body: The 'ask it twice, get two different opinions' disease is exactly why most AI trading tools are useless for anything serious. Your deterministic state.json approach and the agent-never-places-a-trade rule are the right architecture. trademates.co lives on the same side of that split - structured output per ticker (recommendation, risk class, scenarios) instead of free-form chat, no auto-execution. https://trademates.co - US equities only, doesn't touch your NSE market or the Todoist feedback loop you built. Curious how the 200-DMA regime gate performed during the March 2020 gap-down - did it trigger correctly or did the gap skip the exit?

replies.author: Somchandra17
replies.body:
Quick premise fix: the 200-DMA gate is an entry filter, not an exit exits (stop / trend-break / news) are never gated, so there's no gate exit for a gap to skip.  
Honest answer on March 2020: the backtest window is Jul 2023 - May 2026, so it doesn't cover it. From that window: entries above the index 200-SMA ran +6.13% expectancy (n=341) vs −1.08% below (n=28) - small below-sample and bull-heavy window, both flagged in the doc. The harness is re-runnable, so extending back through 2020 is on the list.

On gaps generally: stops evaluate on closes, so the signal can't be skippebut the fill slips to next-day prices. A human places every order, so slippage is the operator's reality, and the backtest's SL-first convention biases against the system deliberately.
